title: Tackling the Macro Picture in Rising Cost of Living Challenges
what_it_is: Tackling the Macro Picture in Rising Cost of Living Challenges

sections.label: Consumer inflation this year
sections.summary: Consumer price inflation has averaged 4.9% this year, more than double the 2.3% rate in 2021.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Since the start of the year, inflation in the prices faced by consumers has averaged 4.9%.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: This is more than double the rate of 2.3% in 2021.

sections.label: MAS on core inflation drivers
sections.summary: MAS said only a third of the rise in core inflation is from external sources and about half from domestic drivers.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: None other than our own MAS has pointed out that only a third of the increase in core inflation is due to external sources, with about half due to domestic drivers.

sections.label: Off-Budget fiscal package measures
sections.summary: The Government has announced a suite of measures in an off-Budget fiscal package, though the speaker believes more can be done.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: While the Government has announced a suite of measures in an off-Budget fiscal package, I believe more can be done at this juncture from a big picture perspective.

sections.label: MAS influence on bond rates
sections.summary: MAS does not directly seek to raise the Singapore cash rate of 0.7% but could influence interest rates for Government bonds maturing 10 years or later.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: This will beat down their prices and, conversely, raise their yield.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Thus, even though MAS does not directly seek to increase the Singapore cash rate – currently at 0.7% – it could, nonetheless, influence interest rates for Government bonds maturing 10 years or later.

sections.label: MAS monetary policy tightening
sections.summary: Minister of State Alvin Tan said MAS is aware of this and has tightened monetary policy thrice since October last year.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: As Minister of State Alvin Tan shared with this House two months ago and again yesterday, MAS is aware of this and had already tightened monetary policy thrice since October last year.

sections.label: US-Singapore dollar exchange rate
sections.summary: The US-Singapore dollar exchange rate was 1.35 on 14 October and 1.40 by mid-June, close to 4% weaker than at the start.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: On 14 October, the day of the first MAS announcement, the exchange rate between the US and Singapore dollar was 1.35.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: As of mid-June, after three separate efforts, this was 1.40 – getting close to 4% weaker than when the exercise first started.

sections.label: Revenue rise versus support package
sections.summary: FY 2021 revenue was $74.8 billion, $13.4 billion above FY 2020, while the announced package is only $1.5 billion.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Revenue for the previous fiscal year, FY 2021, was $74.8 billion – $13.4 billion higher than the fiscal year 2020 and $7.1 billion more than two years ago, before the pandemic.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The jump in property stamp duty alone was $6.8 billion even as personal and corporate income taxes have fully recovered.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Yet, the announced package only amounts to $1.5 billion – a fraction of this revenue increase.

sections.label: Comcare and CPF interest increases
sections.summary: The speaker believes Comcare assistance should be permanently and universally increased and CPF interest rates temporarily raised about two percentage points for six months.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: I believe that Comcare assistance should be permanently and universally increased, by a margin that reflects the excess inflation experienced by families for this year.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: I also believe that we can roll out a temporary increase in CPF interest rates of around two percentage points for a six-month period, consistent with the increase in inflation.

sections.label: Tools to battle inflation
sections.summary: The speaker proposes strengthening the Singapore dollar, buying long bonds, and temporary spending financed by rebating windfall tax gains to battle inflation.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Strengthen the Singapore dollar, because a strong currency makes the stuff we import cheaper.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Buy long bonds, because this will dampen speculative investment and keep a lid on asset prices.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Spend to support those among us that are hurting most for a temporary period and finance this by rebating any windfall tax gains.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: We need to battle inflation proactively and we have the tools to do so.

sections.label: Global versus domestic price rises
sections.summary: Global food and energy prices rose more year-on-year than domestic food prices and Singapore's energy-related CPI components over the same period.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: For global food prices, while global food commodity prices increased by an average of 25.4% year-on-year over the first five months of 2022, domestic food prices increased by an average of 3.6% year-on-year over the same period.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: On energy prices, likewise, even as global energy prices rose by 27.5%, energy-related components in Singapore's Consumer Price Index, which includes the cost of electricity, gas and petrol, increased by 13.6% year-on-year between January and May.

sections.label: Jobs Support Scheme saved jobs
sections.summary: The Jobs Support Scheme, which gave wage subsidies to employers to retain workers, saved 165,000 local jobs between March and December 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: In particular, our Jobs Support Scheme (JSS), which provided wage subsidies to employers to help them retain workers, saved 165,000 local jobs between March and December 2020.

sections.label: June support package for Singaporeans
sections.summary: The additional S$1.5 billion package announced on 21 June provides immediate targeted relief to lower-income and vulnerable Singaporeans affected by higher prices.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: The additional S$1.5 billion support package Deputy Prime Minister Lawrence Wong announced on 21 June provides immediate and targeted relief to lower-income and vulnerable Singaporeans, who are disproportionately affected by higher prices.

sections.label: MAS exchange rate policy
sections.summary: MAS strengthened the exchange rate by at least 5% annually, keeping domestic food inflation at one-fifth of global food inflation.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: MAS, using its monetary policy, has strengthened the exchange rate by at least 5% on an annualised basis, which has kept domestic food inflation, for example, to one-fifth of global food inflation thus far.

sections.label: Fiscal and monetary policy support
sections.summary: The S$1.5 billion package and combined fiscal and monetary policy supported GDP growth and unemployment without adding inflation.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: In fact, the Member mentioned that the fiscal policy must be timely, targeted and temporary in rebating back fiscal upsides.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: That is what we have precisely done with the S$1.5 billion support package.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: If you look at it, the combined Budgets of 2020/2021, together with monetary policy decisions – both fiscal and monetary policy together – supported Singapore's GDP growth by about one percentage point in 2021 and prevented the deterioration of the unemployment rate by four percentage points, even as the combined expansionary monetary macroeconomic policy responses were non-inflationary.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: At this juncture, the current round of combined fiscal and monetary policy responses is expected to contain medium-term inflation, without significant loss of output or inadvertently adding further to the underlying tightness in the economy.
